blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Spatial Error and Clearance Bounds**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, Sensor Perception, § Spatial Error and Clearance Bounds
blocks.md: If perception places a warehouse rack upright just a few centimeters farther from the base's trajectory than it actually stands, the motion planner consumes those missing centimeters directly from its … side clearance, although no stage of the pipeline decided to spend them. Once downstream control logic uses an estimated coordinate to authorize motion, every spatial error becomes a physical displacement drawn from the clearance that protects the robot from collision.

questions.q: The section **Spatial Error and Clearance Bounds** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Spatial error is spent from the same clearance as age, so the clearance inset rests on a measured high quantile of residuals against ground truth, which for stereo grows with range squared.
Out-of-distribution and input-support monitors flag into the health bitmask and can demote a camera to LiDAR-only operation, but they cannot certify what the transducer itself got wrong.
The proposal camera and the admission LiDAR must not share a failure mode, so the metric veto is independent evidence only when its sensing differs from the proposer's.
Fog, rain, glare, and retroreflective vests degrade each modality by its own physics (contrast decay, scattering, blooming, range walk), so a sensor's qualification names its weather.

points: **Spatial error bound**: A qualified bound on measurement and calibration error used to reduce the clearance credited to a motion.
